title: Towards more complete solutions for Lexical Semantic Change: an extension to multiple time periods and diachronic word sense induction
venue: Proceedings of the 5th Workshop on Computational Approaches to Historical Language Change (LChange'24), ACL, pp. 108-119

selection.evidence: Cited as [13] in cassotti2025 for the standard LSC pipeline; its title names the exact setting of SemEval-2027 Task 3 (multiple periods + diachronic WSI) and a task organiser (Tahmasebi) is co-author.

cost.compute_notes: ACL Anthology PDF, 12 pp, read in full. Position paper: no experiments, no artifacts.

triggers: how to cluster word usages across many time periods
one-time clustering vs incremental clustering diachronic word sense induction
consecutive vs cumulative vs pairwise semantic change assessment
cluster alignment across time periods semantic change

claims.statement: Two-period LSC methods do not extend trivially to many periods: re-clustering consecutive intervals breaks 'faithfulness' (usages of t_i are clustered differently with t_{i-1} than with t_{i+1}); one-time clustering over all periods is order-insensitive and lets later periods reshape earlier senses; the authors advocate incremental clustering.
claims.scope: Argument only; five approaches (consecutive intervals, consecutive periods + alignment, one-time over all periods, incremental, form-based scaling) and three assessment settings (consecutive, pairwise, cumulative).

our_assessment.why: The taxonomy is useful and the faithfulness point is right. The preference for incremental clustering is argued, not measured: no experiment compares the five approaches on any gold data. For a benchmark that scores ONE clustering across all periods (SemEval-2027 Task 3 1a, then JSD between consecutive periods for 1b), one-time clustering is the only one of the five that yields a single consistent label space without an alignment step, so 'order-insensitive' is a property the metric does not penalise.

relations.why: Tahmasebi on both; saponara2026 is the first multi-period gold the position paper says is missing.

open_questions: Does incremental clustering beat one-time clustering on a multi-period sense-annotated gold (synthetic EN zenodo 21703081, or the SemEval-2027 Task 3 test after release)? Measurable now on the synthetic set.
